speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Minister for Transport whether he can provide an update on the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit (RTS) Link including the implications of converting the RTS into a Light Rail Transit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The RTS Link is an important bilateral project that will ease Causeway congestion, facilitate business and tourism, and bring our peoples closer together.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: We understand there are a lot of changes in Malaysia recently and it might impact long-term projects between the two countries.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: So, given the context, I have three supplementary questions.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: First, what are the safeguards in ensuring that the RTS Link project will be carried out even if there is a change in government in Malaysia over the next few years?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Second, what are the implications of having the switch of the RTS Link depot from the existing Thomson-East Coast Line's Mandai Depot, to a new depot in Wadi Hana, Johor Bahru?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Does it mean that the maintenance of the RTS Link trains and system will lie primarily in Malaysia and what would be the impact on the reliability of RTS Link?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Ang, can you keep it to two supplementary questions, please.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Would MOT consider building a transfer line along the Causeway to supplement the RTS Link or replace the RTS Link if the RTS Link becomes not viable again?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think Mr Ang is aware that for the RTS Link project, it was suspended for a short while and we had to discuss together with Malaysia on what were the arrangements that were acceptable to both countries.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: In such negotiations and discussions, there will be some give and take, some changes made.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I mentioned earlier, and I stressed this point, 10,000 passengers per hour per direction.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Because that was what we wanted; to make sure that continues to be the case.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, even though we switched from the TEL to LRT, we continue to be able to achieve this objective.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Ang also asked about maintenance, and again, I mentioned this in my main reply.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I said there is a OpCo that is being formed by companies from both sides.
